sanskrit_shloka:
ज्ञानोदयात्पुरारब्धं कर्मज्ञानान्न नश्यति ।
अदत्वा स्वफलं लक्ष्यमुद्दिश्योत्सृष्टबाणवत् ॥ ४५१ ॥
transliteration:
jñānodayātpurārabdhaṃ karmajñānānna naśyati |
adatvā svaphalaṃ lakṣyamuddiśyotsṛṣṭabāṇavat || 451 ||
translation: The work which has fashioned this body prior to the dawning of knowledge, is not destroyed by that knowledge without yielding its fruits, like the arrow shot at an object.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The work which has fashioned this body prior to the dawning of knowledge, is not destroyed by that knowledge without yielding its fruits, like the arrow shot at an object.

sanskrit_shloka:
व्याघ्रबुद्ध्या विनिर्मुक्तो बाणः पश्चात्तु गोमतौ ।
न तिष्ठति छिनत्येव लक्ष्यं वेगेन निर्भरम् ॥ ४५२ ॥
transliteration:
vyāghrabuddhyā vinirmukto bāṇaḥ paścāttu gomatau |
na tiṣṭhati chinatyeva lakṣyaṃ vegena nirbharam || 452 ||
translation: The arrow which is shot at an object with the idea that it is a tiger, does not, when that object is perceived to be a cow, check itself, but pierces the object with full force.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The arrow which is shot at an object with the idea that it is a tiger, does not, when that object is perceived to be a cow, check itself, but pierces the object with full force.

sanskrit_shloka:
प्राब्धं बलवत्तरं खलु विदां भोगेन तस्य क्षयः सम्यग्ज्ञानहुताशनेन विलयः प्राक्षंचितागामिनाम् ।
ब्रह्मात्मैक्यमवेक्ष्य तन्मायातया ये सर्वदा संस्थिताः तेषां तत्त्रितयं नहि क्वचिदपि ब्रह्मैव ते निर्गुणम् ॥ ४५३ ॥
transliteration:
prābdhaṃ balavattaraṃ khalu vidāṃ bhogena tasya kṣayaḥ samyagjñānahutāśanena vilayaḥ prākṣaṃcitāgāminām |
brahmātmaikyamavekṣya tanMāyātayā ye sarvadā saṃsthitāḥ teṣāṃ tattritayaṃ nahi kvacidapi brahmaiva te nirguṇam || 453 ||
translation: Prārabdha work is certainly very strong for the man of realisation, and is spent only by the actual experience of its fruit; while the actions previously accumulated and those yet to come are destroyed by the fire of perfect knowledge. But none of the three at all affects those who, realising their identity with Brahman, are always living absorbed in that idea. They are verily the transcendent Brahman.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Prārabdha work is certainly very strong for the man of realisation, and is spent only by the actual experience of its fruit; while the actions previously accumulated and those yet to come are destroyed by the fire of perfect knowledge. But none of the three at all affects those who, realising their identity with Brahman, are always living absorbed in that idea. They are verily the transcendent Brahman.

sanskrit_shloka:
उपाधितादात्म्यविहीनकेवल ब्रह्मात्मनैवात्मनि तिष्ठतो मुनेः ।
प्रारब्धसद्भावकथा न युक्ता स्वप्नार्थसंबन्धकथेव जाग्रतः ॥ ४५४ ॥
transliteration:
upādhitādātmyavihīnakevala brahmātmanaivātmani tiṣṭhato muneḥ |
prārabdhasadbhāvakathā na yuktā svapnārthasaṃbandhakatheva jāgrataḥ || 454 ||
translation: For the sage who lives in his own Self as Brahman, the One without a second, devoid of identification with the limiting adjuncts, the question of the existence of Prārabdha work is meaningless, like the question of a man who has awakened from sleep having any connection with the objects seen in the dream-state.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: For the sage who lives in his own Self as Brahman, the One without a second, devoid of identification with the limiting adjuncts, the question of the existence of Prārabdha work is meaningless, like the question of a man who has awakened from sleep having any connection with the objects seen in the dream-state.

sanskrit_shloka:
न हि प्रबुद्धः प्रतिभासदेहे देहोपयोगिन्यपि च प्रपञ्चे ।
करोत्यहन्तां ममतानिदन्तां किन्तु स्वयं तिष्ठति जागरेण ॥ ४५५ ॥
transliteration:
na hi prabuddhaḥ pratibhāsadehe dehopayoginyapi ca prapañce |
karotyahantāṃ mamatānidantāṃ kintu svayaṃ tiṣṭhati jāgareṇa || 455 ||
translation: The man who has awakened from sleep never has any idea of 'I' or 'mine' with regard to his dream-body and the dream-objects that ministered to that body, but lives quite awake, as his own Self.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The man who has awakened from sleep never has any idea of 'I' or 'mine' with regard to his dream-body and the dream-objects that ministered to that body, but lives quite awake, as his own Self.

sanskrit_shloka:
न तस्य मिथ्यार्थसमर्थनेच्छा न संग्रहस्तज्जगतोऽपि दृष्टः ।
तत्रानुवृत्तिर्यदि चेन्मृषार्थे न निद्रया मुक्त इतीष्यते ध्रुवम् ॥ ४५६ ॥
transliteration:
na tasya mithyārthasamarthanecchā na saṃgrahastajjagato'pi dṛṣṭaḥ |
tatrānuvṛttiryadi cenmṛṣārthe na nidrayā mukta itīṣyate dhruvam || 456 ||
translation: He has no desire to substantiate the unreal objects, nor is he seen to maintain that dream-world. If he still clings to those unreal objects, he is emphatically declared to be not yet free from sleep.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: He has no desire to substantiate the unreal objects, nor is he seen to maintain that dream-world. If he still clings to those unreal objects, he is emphatically declared to be not yet free from sleep.

sanskrit_shloka:
तद्वत्परे ब्रह्मणि वर्तमानः सदात्मना तिष्ठति नान्यदीक्षते ।
स्मृतिर्यथा स्वप्नविलोकितार्थे तथा विदः प्राशनमोचनादौ ॥ ४५७ ॥
transliteration:
tadvatpare brahmaṇi vartamānaḥ sadātmanā tiṣṭhati nānyadīkṣate |
smṛtiryathā svapnavilokitārthe tathā vidaḥ prāśanamocanādau || 457 ||
translation: Similarly, he who is absorbed in Brahman lives identified with that eternal Reality and beholds nothing else. As one has a memory of the objects seen in a dream, so the man of realisation has a memory of the everyday actions such as eating.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Similarly, he who is absorbed in Brahman lives identified with that eternal Reality and beholds nothing else. As one has a memory of the objects seen in a dream, so the man of realisation has a memory of the everyday actions such as eating.

sanskrit_shloka:
कर्मणा निर्मितो देहः प्रारब्धं तस्य कल्प्यताम् ।
नानादेरात्मनो युक्तं नैवात्मा कर्मनिर्मितः ॥ ४५८ ॥
transliteration:
karmaṇā nirmito dehaḥ prārabdhaṃ tasya kalpyatām |
nānāderātmano yuktaṃ naivātmā karmanirmitaḥ || 458 ||
translation: The body has been fashioned by Karma, so one may imagine Prarabdha work with reference to it. But it is not reasonable to attribute the same to the Ātman, for the Ātman is never the outcome of work.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The body has been fashioned by Karma, so one may imagine Prarabdha work with reference to it. But it is not reasonable to attribute the same to the Ātman, for the Ātman is never the outcome of work.

sanskrit_shloka:
अजो नित्यः शाश्वत इति ब्रूते श्रुतिरमोघवाक् ।
तदात्मना तिष्ठतोऽस्य कुतः प्रारब्धकल्पना ॥ ४५९ ॥
transliteration:
ajo nityaḥ śāśvata iti brūte śrutiramoghavāk |
tadātmanā tiṣṭhato'sya kutaḥ prārabdhakalpanā || 459 ||
translation: The Śrutis, whose words are infallible, declare the Ātman to be 'birthless, eternal and undecaying'. So, the man who lives identified with That, how can Prārabdha work be attributed?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The Śrutis, whose words are infallible, declare the Ātman to be 'birthless, eternal and undecaying'. So, the man who lives identified with That, how can Prārabdha work be attributed?

sanskrit_shloka:
प्रारब्धं सिध्यति तदा यदा देहात्मना स्थितिः ।
देहात्मभावो नैवेष्टः प्रारब्धं त्यज्यतामतः ॥ ४६0 ॥
transliteration:
prārabdhaṃ sidhyati tadā yadā dehātmanā sthitiḥ |
dehātmabhāvo naiveṣṭaḥ prārabdhaṃ tyajyatāmataḥ || 460 ||
translation: Prārabdha work can be maintained only so long as one lives identified with the body. But no one admits that the man of realisation ever identifies himself with the body. Hence Prārabdha work should be rejected in his case.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Prārabdha work can be maintained only so long as one lives identified with the body. But no one admits that the man of realisation ever identifies himself with the body. Hence Prārabdha work should be rejected in his case.

sanskrit_shloka:
शरीरस्यापि प्रारब्धकल्पना भ्रान्तिरेव हि ।
अध्यस्तस्य कुतः सत्त्वमसत्यस्य कुतो जनिः अजातस्य कुतो नाशः प्रारब्धमसतः कुतः ॥ ४६१ ॥
transliteration:
śarīrasyāpi prārabdhakalpanā bhrāntireva hi |
adhyastasya kutaḥ sattvamasatyasya kuto janiḥ ajātasya kuto nāśaḥ prārabdhamasataḥ kutaḥ || 461 ||
translation: The attributing of Prārabdha work to the body even is certainly an error. How can something that is superimposed (on another) have any existence, and how can that which is unreal have a birth? And how can that which has not been born at all, die? So how can Prārabdha work exist for something that is unreal?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The attributing of Prārabdha work to the body even is certainly an error. How can something that is superimposed (on another) have any existence, and how can that which is unreal have a birth? And how can that which has not been born at all, die? So how can Prārabdha work exist for something that is unreal?

sanskrit_shloka:
ज्ञानेनाज्ञानकार्यस्य समूलस्य लयो यदि ।
तिष्ठत्ययं कथं देह इति शङ्कावतो जडान् ॥ ४६२ ॥ समाधातुं बाह्यदृष्ट्या प्रारब्धं वदति श्रुतिः ।
न तु देहादिसत्यत्वबोधनाय विपश्चिताम् ॥ ४६३ ॥
transliteration:
jñānenājñānakāryasya samūlasya layo yadi |
tiṣṭhatyayaṃ kathaṃ deha iti śaṅkāvato jaḍān || 462 || samādhātuṃ bāhyadṛṣṭyā prārabdhaṃ vadati śrutiḥ |
na tu dehādisatyatvabodhanāya vipaścitām || 463 ||
translation: 462-463. 'If the effects of ignorance are destroyed with their root by knowledge, then how does the body live?' – it is to convince those fools who entertain a doubt like this, that the Śrutis, from a relative standpoint, hypothesise Prārabdha work, but not for proving the reality of the body etc., of the man of realisation.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: 462-463. 'If the effects of ignorance are destroyed with their root by knowledge, then how does the body live?' – it is to convince those fools who entertain a doubt like this, that the Śrutis, from a relative standpoint, hypothesise Prārabdha work, but not for proving the reality of the body etc., of the man of realisation.

sanskrit_shloka:
परिपूर्णमनाद्यन्तमप्रमेयमविक्रियम् ।
एकमेवाद्वयं ब्रह्म नेह नानास्ति किंचन ॥ ४६४ ॥
transliteration:
paripūrṇamanādyantamaprameyamavikriyam |
ekamevādvayaṃ brahma neha nānāsti kiṃcana || 464 ||
translation: There is only Brahman, the One without a second, infinite, without beginning or end, transcendent and changeless; there is no duality whatsoever in It.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: There is only Brahman, the One without a second, infinite, without beginning or end, transcendent and changeless; there is no duality whatsoever in It.

sanskrit_shloka:
परिपूर्णमनाद्यन्तमप्रमेयमविक्रियम् ।
एकमेवाद्वयं ब्रह्म नेह नानास्ति किंचन ॥ ४६४ ॥
transliteration:
paripūrṇamanādyantamaprameyamavikriyam |
ekamevādvayaṃ brahma neha nānāsti kiṃcana || 464 ||
translation: There is only Brahman, the One without a second, infinite, without beginning or end, transcendent and changeless; there is no duality whatsoever in It.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: There is only Brahman, the One without a second, infinite, without beginning or end, transcendent and changeless; there is no duality whatsoever in It.

sanskrit_shloka:
सद्गनं चिद्घनं नित्यमानन्दघनमक्रियम् ।
एकमेवाद्वयं ब्रह्म नेह नानास्ति किंचन ॥ ४६५ ॥
transliteration:
sadganaṃ cidghanaṃ nityamānandaghanamakriyam |
ekamevādvayaṃ brahma neha nānāsti kiṃcana || 465 ||
translation: There is only Brahman, the One without a second, the Essence of Existence, Knowledge and Eternal Bliss, and devoid of activity; there is no duality whatsoever in It.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: There is only Brahman, the One without a second, the Essence of Existence, Knowledge and Eternal Bliss, and devoid of activity; there is no duality whatsoever in It.

sanskrit_shloka:
प्रत्यगेकरसं पूर्णमनन्तं सर्वतोमुखम् ।
एकमेवाद्वयं ब्रह्म नेह नानास्ति किंचन ॥ ४६६ ॥
transliteration:
pratyagekarasaṃ pūrṇamanantaṃ sarvatomukham |
ekamevādvayaṃ brahma neha nānāsti kiṃcana || 466 ||
translation: There is only Brahman, the One without a second, which is within all, homogeneous, infinite, endless, and all-pervading; there is no duality whatsoever in It.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: There is only Brahman, the One without a second, which is within all, homogeneous, infinite, endless, and all-pervading; there is no duality whatsoever in It.

sanskrit_shloka:
अहेयमनुपादेयमनादेयमनाश्रयम् ।
एकमेवाद्वयं ब्रह्म नेह नानास्ति किंचन ॥ ४६७ ॥
transliteration:
aheyamanupādeyamanādeyamanāśrayam |
ekamevādvayaṃ brahma neha nānāsti kiṃcana || 467 ||
translation: There is only Brahman, the One without a second, which is neither to be shunned nor taken up nor accepted, and which is without any support, there is no duality whatsoever in It.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: There is only Brahman, the One without a second, which is neither to be shunned nor taken up nor accepted, and which is without any support, there is no duality whatsoever in It.

sanskrit_shloka:
निर्गुणं निष्कलं सूक्ष्मं निर्विकल्पं निरञ्जनम् ।
एकमेवाद्वयं ब्रह्म नेह नानास्ति किंचन ॥ ४६८ ॥
transliteration:
nirguṇaṃ niṣkalaṃ sūkṣmaṃ nirvikalpaṃ nirañjanam |
ekamevādvayaṃ brahma neha nānāsti kiṃcana || 468 ||
translation: There is only Brahman, the One without a second, beyond attributes, without parts, subtle, absolute and taintless; there is no duality whatsoever in It.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: There is only Brahman, the One without a second, beyond attributes, without parts, subtle, absolute and taintless; there is no duality whatsoever in It.

sanskrit_shloka:
अनिरूप्य स्वरूपं यन्मनोवाचामगोचरम् ।
एकमेवाद्वयं ब्रह्म नेह नानास्ति किंचन ॥ ४६९ ॥
transliteration:
anirūpya svarūpaṃ yanmanovācāmagocaram |
ekamevādvayaṃ brahma neha nānāsti kiṃcana || 469 ||
translation: There is only Brahman, the One without a second, whose real nature is incomprehensible, and which is beyond the range of mind and speech; there is no duality whatsoever in It.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: There is only Brahman, the One without a second, whose real nature is incomprehensible, and which is beyond the range of mind and speech; there is no duality whatsoever in It.

sanskrit_shloka:
सत्समृद्धं स्वतःसिद्धं शुद्धं बुद्धमनीदृशम् ।
एकमेवाद्वयं ब्रह्म नेह नानास्ति किंचन ॥ ४७0 ॥
transliteration:
satsamṛddhaṃ svataḥsiddhaṃ śuddhaṃ buddhamanīdṛśam |
ekamevādvayaṃ brahma neha nānāsti kiṃcana || 470 ||
translation: There is only Brahman, the One without a second, the Reality, the One without a second, the Reality, effulgent, self-existent, pure, intelligent, and unlike anything finite; there is no duality whatsoever in It.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: There is only Brahman, the One without a second, the Reality, the One without a second, the Reality, effulgent, self-existent, pure, intelligent, and unlike anything finite; there is no duality whatsoever in It.

sanskrit_shloka:
निरस्तरागा विनिरस्तभोगाः शान्ताः सुदान्ता यतयो महान्तः ।
विज्ञाय तत्त्वं परमेतदन्ते प्राप्ताः परां निर्वृतिमात्मयोगात् ॥ ४७१ ॥
transliteration:
nirastarāgā vinirastabhogāḥ śāntāḥ sudāntā yatayo mahāntaḥ |
vijñāya tattvaṃ parametadante prāptāḥ parāṃ nirvṛtimātmayogāt || 471 ||
translation: High-souled Sannyasins who have got rid of all attachment and discarded all sense- enjoyments, and who are serene and perfectly restrained, realise this Supreme Truth and at the end attain the Supreme Bliss through their Self-realisation.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: High-souled Sannyasins who have got rid of all attachment and discarded all sense- enjoyments, and who are serene and perfectly restrained, realise this Supreme Truth and at the end attain the Supreme Bliss through their Self-realisation.

sanskrit_shloka:
भवानपीदं परतत्त्वमात्मनः स्वरूपमानन्दघनं विचार्य ।
विधूय मोहं स्वमनःप्रकल्पितं मुक्तः कृतार्थो भवतु प्रबुद्धः ॥ ४७२ ॥
transliteration:
bhavānapīdaṃ paratattvamātmanaḥ svarūpamānandaghanaṃ vicārya |
vidhūya mohaṃ svamanaḥprakalpitaṃ muktaḥ kṛtārtho bhavatu prabuddhaḥ || 472 ||
translation: Thou, too, discriminate this Supreme Truth, the real nature of the Self, which is Bliss undiluted, and shaking off thy delusion created by thy own mind, be free and illumined, and attain the consummation of thy life.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Thou, too, discriminate this Supreme Truth, the real nature of the Self, which is Bliss undiluted, and shaking off thy delusion created by thy own mind, be free and illumined, and attain the consummation of thy life.

sanskrit_shloka:
समाधिना साधुविनिश्चलात्मना पश्यात्मतत्त्वं स्फुटबोधचक्षुषा ।
निःसंशयं सम्यगवेक्षितश्चेच् छ्रुतः पदार्थो न पुनर्विकल्प्यते ॥ ४७३ ॥
transliteration:
samādhinā sādhuviniścalātmanā paśyātmatattvaṃ sphuṭabodhacakṣuṣā |
niḥsaṃśayaṃ samyagavekṣitaścec chrutaḥ padārtho na punarvikalpyate || 473 ||
translation: Through the Samadhi in which the mind has been perfectly stilled, visualise the Truth of the Self with the eye of clear realisation. If the meaning of the (Scriptural) words heard from the Guru is perfectly and indubitably discerned, then it can lead to no more doubt.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Through the Samadhi in which the mind has been perfectly stilled, visualise the Truth of the Self with the eye of clear realisation. If the meaning of the (Scriptural) words heard from the Guru is perfectly and indubitably discerned, then it can lead to no more doubt.

sanskrit_shloka:
स्वस्याविद्याबन्धसंबन्धमोक्षात् सत्यज्ञानानन्दरूपात्मलब्धौ ।
शास्त्रं युक्तिर्देशिकोक्तिः प्रमाणं चान्तःसिद्धा स्वानुभूतिः प्रमाणम् ॥ ४७४ ॥
transliteration:
svasyāvidyābandhasaṃbandhamokṣāt satyajñānānandarūpātmalabdhau |
śāstraṃ yuktirdeśikoktiḥ pramāṇaṃ cāntaḥsiddhā svānubhūtiḥ pramāṇam || 474 ||
translation: In the realisation of the Ātman, the Existence-Knowledge-Bliss Absolute, through the breaking of one’s connection with the bondage of Avidya or ignorance, the Scriptures, reasoning and the words of the Guru are the proofs, while one’s own experience earned by concentrating the mind is another proof.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: In the realisation of the Ātman, the Existence-Knowledge-Bliss Absolute, through the breaking of one’s connection with the bondage of Avidya or ignorance, the Scriptures, reasoning and the words of the Guru are the proofs, while one’s own experience earned by concentrating the mind is another proof.

sanskrit_shloka:
बन्धो मोक्षश्च तृप्तिश्च चिन्तारोग्यक्षुदादयः ।
स्वेनैव वेद्या यज्ज्ञानं परेषामानुमानिकम् ॥ ४७५ ॥
transliteration:
bandho mokṣaśca tṛptiśca cintārogyakṣudādayaḥ |
svenaiva vedyā yajjñānaṃ pareṣāmānumānikam || 475 ||
translation: Bondage, liberation, satisfaction, anxiety, recovery from illness, hunger and other such things are known only to the man concerned, and knowledge of these to others is a mere inference.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Bondage, liberation, satisfaction, anxiety, recovery from illness, hunger and other such things are known only to the man concerned, and knowledge of these to others is a mere inference.

sanskrit_shloka:
तटस्थिता बोधयन्ति गुरवः श्रुतयो यथा ।
प्रज्ञयैव तरेद्विद्वानीश्वरानुगृहीतया ॥ ४७६ ॥
transliteration:
taṭasthitā bodhayanti guravaḥ śrutayo yathā |
prajñayaiva taredvidvānīśvarānugṛhītayā || 476 ||
translation: The Gurus as well as the Śrutis instruct the disciple, standing aloof; while the man of realisation crosses (Avidya) through Illumination alone, backed by the grace of God.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The Gurus as well as the Śrutis instruct the disciple, standing aloof; while the man of realisation crosses (Avidya) through Illumination alone, backed by the grace of God.

sanskrit_shloka:
स्वानुभूत्या स्वयं ज्ञात्वा स्वमात्मानमखण्डितम् ।
संसिद्धः संमुखं तिष्ठेन्निर्विकल्पात्मनात्मनि ॥ ४७७ ॥
transliteration:
svānubhūtyā svayaṃ jñātvā svamātmānamakhaṇḍitam |
saṃsiddhaḥ saṃmukhaṃ tiṣṭhennirvikalpātmanātmani || 477 ||
translation: Himself knowing his indivisible Self through his own realisation and thus becoming perfect, a man should stand face to face with the Ātman, with his mind free from dualistic ideas.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Himself knowing his indivisible Self through his own realisation and thus becoming perfect, a man should stand face to face with the Ātman, with his mind free from dualistic ideas.

sanskrit_shloka:
वेदान्तसिद्धान्तनिरुक्तिरेषा ब्रह्मैव जीवः सकलं जगच्च ।
अखण्डरूपस्थितिरेव मोक्षो ब्रह्माद्वितीये श्रुतयः प्रमाणम् ॥ ४७८ ॥
transliteration:
vedāntasiddhāntaniruktireṣā brahmaiva jīvaḥ sakalaṃ jagacca |
akhaṇḍarūpasthitireva mokṣo brahmādvitīye śrutayaḥ pramāṇam || 478 ||
translation: The verdict of all discussions on the Vedanta is that the Jīva and the whole universe are nothing but Brahman, and that liberation means abiding in Brahman, the indivisible Entity. While the Śrutis themselves are authority (for the statement) that Brahman is One without a second.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The verdict of all discussions on the Vedanta is that the Jīva and the whole universe are nothing but Brahman, and that liberation means abiding in Brahman, the indivisible Entity. While the Śrutis themselves are authority (for the statement) that Brahman is One without a second.

sanskrit_shloka:
इति गुरुवचनाच्छ्रुतिप्रमाणात् परमवगम्य सतत्त्वमात्मयुक्त्या ।
प्रशमितकरणः समाहितात्मा क्वचिदचलाकृतिरात्मनिष्ठतोऽभूत् ॥ ४७९ ॥
transliteration:
iti guruvacanācchrutipramāṇāt paramavagamya satattvamātmayuktyā |
praśamitakaraṇaḥ samāhitātmā kvacidacalākṛtirātmaniṣṭhato'bhūt || 479 ||
translation: Realising, at a blessed moment, the Supreme Truth through the above instructions of the Guru, the authority of the Scriptures and his own reasoning, with his senses quieted and the mind concentrated, (the disciple) became immovable in form and perfectly established in the Ātman.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Realising, at a blessed moment, the Supreme Truth through the above instructions of the Guru, the authority of the Scriptures and his own reasoning, with his senses quieted and the mind concentrated, (the disciple) became immovable in form and perfectly established in the Ātman.

sanskrit_shloka:
किंचित्कालं समाधाय परे ब्रह्मणि मानसम् ।
उत्थाय परमानन्दादिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ ४८0 ॥
transliteration:
kiṃcitkālaṃ samādhāya pare brahmaṇi mānasam |
utthāya paramānandādidaṃ vacanamabravīt || 480 ||
translation: Concentrating the mind for some time on the Supreme Brahman, he rose, and out of supreme bliss spoke as follows.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Concentrating the mind for some time on the Supreme Brahman, he rose, and out of supreme bliss spoke as follows.

sanskrit_shloka:
बुद्धिर्विनष्टा गलिता प्रवृत्तिः ब्रह्मात्मनोरेकतयाधिगत्या ।
इदं न जानेऽप्यनिदं न जाने किं वा कियद्वा सुखमस्त्यपारम् ॥ ४८१ ॥
transliteration:
buddhirvinaṣṭā galitā pravṛttiḥ brahmātmanorekatayādhigatyā |
idaṃ na jāne'pyanidaṃ na jāne kiṃ vā kiyadvā sukhamastyapāram || 481 ||
translation: My mind has vanished, and all its activities have melted, by realising the identity of the Self and Brahman; I do not know either this or not-this; nor what or how much the boundless Bliss (of Samadhi) is!

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: My mind has vanished, and all its activities have melted, by realising the identity of the Self and Brahman; I do not know either this or not-this; nor what or how much the boundless Bliss (of Samadhi) is!

sanskrit_shloka:
वाचा वक्तुमशक्यमेव मनसा मन्तुं न वा शक्यते स्वानन्दामृतपूरपूरितपरब्रह्माम्बुधेर्वैभवम् ।
अम्भोराशिविशीर्णवार्षिकशिलाभावं भजन्मे मनो यस्यांशांशलवे विलीनमधुनानन्दात्मना निर्वृतम् ॥ ४८२ ॥
transliteration:
vācā vaktumaśakyameva manasā mantuṃ na vā śakyate svānandāmṛtapūrapūritaparabrahmāmbudhervaibhavam |
ambhorāśiviśīrṇavārṣikaśilābhāvaṃ bhajanme mano yasyāṃśāṃśalave vilīnamadhunānandātmanā nirvṛtam || 482 ||
translation: The majesty of the ocean of Supreme Brahman, replete with the swell of the nectar-like Bliss of the Self, is verily impossible to express in speech, nor can it be conceived by the mind – in an infinitesimal fraction of which my mind melted like a hailstone getting merged in the ocean, and is now satisfied with that Essence of Bliss.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: The majesty of the ocean of Supreme Brahman, replete with the swell of the nectar-like Bliss of the Self, is verily impossible to express in speech, nor can it be conceived by the mind – in an infinitesimal fraction of which my mind melted like a hailstone getting merged in the ocean, and is now satisfied with that Essence of Bliss.

sanskrit_shloka:
क्व गतं केन वा नीतं कुत्र लीनमिदं जगत् ।
अधुनैव मया दृष्टं नास्ति किं महदद्भुतम् ॥ ४८३ ॥
transliteration:
kva gataṃ kena vā nītaṃ kutra līnamidaṃ jagat |
adhunaiva mayā dṛṣṭaṃ nāsti kiṃ mahadadbhutam || 483 ||
translation: Where is the universe gone, by whom is it removed, and where is it merged? It was just now seen by me, and has it ceased to exist? It is passing strange!

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Where is the universe gone, by whom is it removed, and where is it merged? It was just now seen by me, and has it ceased to exist? It is passing strange!

sanskrit_shloka:
किं हेयं किमुपादेयं किमन्यत्किं विलक्षणम् ।
अखण्डानन्दपीयूषपूर्णे ब्रह्ममहार्णवे ॥ ४८४ ॥
transliteration:
kiṃ heyaṃ kimupādeyaṃ kimanyatkiṃ vilakṣaṇam |
akhaṇḍānandapīyūṣapūrṇe brahmamahārṇave || 484 ||
translation: In the ocean of Brahman filled with the nectar of Absolute Bliss, what is to be shunned and what accepted, what is other (than oneself) and what different?

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: In the ocean of Brahman filled with the nectar of Absolute Bliss, what is to be shunned and what accepted, what is other (than oneself) and what different?

sanskrit_shloka:
न किंचिदत्र पश्यामि न शृणोमि न वेद्म्यहम् ।
स्वात्मनैव सदानन्दरूपेणास्मि विलक्षणः ॥ ४८५ ॥
transliteration:
na kiṃcidatra paśyāmi na śṛṇomi na vedmyaham |
svātmanaiva sadānandarūpeṇāsmi vilakṣaṇaḥ || 485 ||
translation: I neither see nor hear nor know anything in this. I simply exist as the Self, the eternal Bliss, distinct from everything else.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: I neither see nor hear nor know anything in this. I simply exist as the Self, the eternal Bliss, distinct from everything else.

sanskrit_shloka:
नमो नमस्ते गुरवे महात्मने विमुक्तसङ्गाय सदुत्तमाय ।
नित्याद्वयानन्दरसस्वरूपिणे भूम्ने सदापारदयाम्बुधाम्ने ॥ ४८६ ॥
transliteration:
namo namaste gurave mahātmane vimuktasaṅgāya saduttamāya |
nityādvayānandarasasvarūpiṇe bhūmne sadāpāradayāmbudhāmne || 486 ||
translation: Repeated salutations to thee, O noble Teacher, who art devoid of attachment, the best among the good souls and the embodiment of the essence of Eternal Bliss, the One without a second – who art infinite and ever the boundless ocean of mercy:

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Repeated salutations to thee, O noble Teacher, who art devoid of attachment, the best among the good souls and the embodiment of the essence of Eternal Bliss, the One without a second – who art infinite and ever the boundless ocean of mercy:

sanskrit_shloka:
यत्कटाक्षशशिसान्द्रचन्द्रिका पातधूतभवतापजश्रमः ।
प्राप्तवानहमखण्डवैभवा नन्दमात्मपदमक्षयं क्षणात् ॥ ४८७ ॥
transliteration:
yatkaṭākṣaśaśisāndracandrikā pātadhūtabhavatāpajaśramaḥ |
prāptavānahamakhaṇḍavaibhavā nandamātmapadamakṣayaṃ kṣaṇāt || 487 ||
translation: Whose glance, like the shower of concentrated moonbeams, has removed my exhaustion brought on by the afflictions of the world, and in a moment admitted me to the undecaying status of the Ātman, the Bliss of infinite majesty!

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Whose glance, like the shower of concentrated moonbeams, has removed my exhaustion brought on by the afflictions of the world, and in a moment admitted me to the undecaying status of the Ātman, the Bliss of infinite majesty!

sanskrit_shloka:
धन्योऽहं कृतकृत्योऽहं विमुक्तोऽहं भवग्रहात् ।
नित्यानन्दस्वरूपोऽहं पूर्णोऽहं त्वदनुग्रहात् ॥ ४८८ ॥
transliteration:
dhanyo'haṃ kṛtakṛtyo'haṃ vimukto'haṃ bhavagrahāt |
nityānandasvarūpo'haṃ pūrṇo'haṃ tvadanugrahāt || 488 ||
translation: Blessed am I; I have attained the consummation of my life, and am free from the clutches of transmigration; I am the Essence of Eternal Bliss, I am infinite – all through thy mercy!

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Blessed am I; I have attained the consummation of my life, and am free from the clutches of transmigration; I am the Essence of Eternal Bliss, I am infinite – all through thy mercy!

sanskrit_shloka:
असङ्गोऽहमनङ्गोऽहमलिङ्गोऽहमभङ्गुरः ।
प्रशान्तोऽहमनन्तोऽहममलोऽहं चिरन्तनः ॥ ४८९ ॥
transliteration:
asaṅgo'hamanaṅgo'hamaliṅgo'hamabhaṅguraḥ |
praśānto'hamananto'hamamalo'haṃ cirantanaḥ || 489 ||
translation: I am unattached, I am disembodied, I am free from the subtle body, and undecaying, I am serene, I am infinite, I am taintless and eternal.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: I am unattached, I am disembodied, I am free from the subtle body, and undecaying, I am serene, I am infinite, I am taintless and eternal.

sanskrit_shloka:
अकर्ताहमभोक्ताहमविकारोऽहमक्रियः ।
शुद्धबोधस्वरूपोऽहं केवलोऽहं सदाशिवः ॥ ४९0 ॥
transliteration:
akartāhamabhoktāhamavikāro'hamakriyaḥ |
śuddhabodhasvarūpo'haṃ kevalo'haṃ sadāśivaḥ || 490 ||
translation: I am not the doer, I am not the experiencer, I am changeless and beyond activity; I am the essence of Pure Knowledge; I am Absolute and identified with Eternal Good.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: I am not the doer, I am not the experiencer, I am changeless and beyond activity; I am the essence of Pure Knowledge; I am Absolute and identified with Eternal Good.

sanskrit_shloka:
द्रष्टुः श्रोतुर्वक्तुः कर्तुर्भोक्तुर्विभिन्न एवाहम् ।
नित्यनिरन्तरनिष्क्रियनिःसीमासङ्गपूर्णबोधात्मा ॥ ४९१ ॥
transliteration:
draṣṭuḥ śroturvaktuḥ karturbhokturvibhinna evāham |
nityanirantaraniṣkriyaniḥsīmāsaṅgapūrṇabodhātmā || 491 ||
translation: I am indeed different from the seer, listener, speaker, doer and experiencer; I am the essence of Knowledge, eternal, without any break, beyond activity, limitless, unattached and infinite.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: I am indeed different from the seer, listener, speaker, doer and experiencer; I am the essence of Knowledge, eternal, without any break, beyond activity, limitless, unattached and infinite.

sanskrit_shloka:
नाहमिदं नाहमदोऽप्युभयोरवभासकं परं शुद्धम् ।
बाह्याभ्यन्तरशून्यं पूर्णं ब्रह्माद्वितीयमेवाहम् ॥ ४९२ ॥
transliteration:
nāhamidaṃ nāhamado'pyubhayoravabhāsakaṃ paraṃ śuddham |
bāhyābhyantaraśūnyaṃ pūrṇaṃ brahmādvitīyamevāham || 492 ||
translation: I am neither, this nor that, but the Supreme, the illuminer of both; I am indeed Brahman, the One without a second, pure, devoid of interior or exterior and infinite.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: I am neither, this nor that, but the Supreme, the illuminer of both; I am indeed Brahman, the One without a second, pure, devoid of interior or exterior and infinite.

sanskrit_shloka:
निरुपममनादितत्त्वं त्वमहमिदमद इति कल्पनादूरम् ।
नित्यानन्दैकरसं सत्यं ब्रह्माद्वितीयमेवाहम् ॥ ४९३ ॥
transliteration:
nirupamamanāditattvaṃ tvamahamidamada iti kalpanādūram |
nityānandaikarasaṃ satyaṃ brahmādvitīyamevāham || 493 ||
translation: I am indeed Brahman, the One without a second, matchless, the Reality that has no beginning, beyond such imagination as thou or I, or this or that, the Essence of Eternal Bliss, the Truth.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: I am indeed Brahman, the One without a second, matchless, the Reality that has no beginning, beyond such imagination as thou or I, or this or that, the Essence of Eternal Bliss, the Truth.

sanskrit_shloka:
नारायणोऽहं नरकान्तकोऽहं पुरान्तकोऽहं पुरुषोऽहमीशः ।
अखण्डबोधोऽहमशेषसाक्षी निरीश्वरोऽहं निरहं च निर्ममः ॥ ४९४ ॥
transliteration:
nārāyaṇo'haṃ narakāntako'haṃ purāntako'haṃ puruṣo'hamīśaḥ |
akhaṇḍabodho'hamaśeṣasākṣī nirīśvaro'haṃ nirahaṃ ca nirmamaḥ || 494 ||
translation: I am Nārāyaṇa, the slayer of Nāraka; I am the destroyer of Tripura, the Supreme Being, the Ruler; I am knowledge Absolute, the Witness of everything; I have no other Ruler but myself, I am devoid of the ideas of 'I’ and 'mine'.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: I am Nārāyaṇa, the slayer of Nāraka; I am the destroyer of Tripura, the Supreme Being, the Ruler; I am knowledge Absolute, the Witness of everything; I have no other Ruler but myself, I am devoid of the ideas of 'I’ and 'mine'.

sanskrit_shloka:
सर्वेषु भूतेष्वहमेव संस्थितो ज्ञानात्मनान्तर्बहिराश्रयः सन् ।
भोक्ता च भोग्यं स्वयमेव सर्वं यद्यत्पृथग्दृष्टमिदन्तया पुरा ॥ ४९५ ॥
transliteration:
sarveṣu bhūteṣvahameva saṃsthito jñānātmanāntarbahirāśrayaḥ san |
bhoktā ca bhogyaṃ svayameva sarvaṃ yadyatpṛthagdṛṣṭamidantayā purā || 495 ||
translation: I alone reside as knowledge in all beings, being their internal and external support. I myself am the experiencer and all that is experienced – whatever I looked upon as 'this' or the not-Self previously.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: I alone reside as knowledge in all beings, being their internal and external support. I myself am the experiencer and all that is experienced – whatever I looked upon as 'this' or the not-Self previously.

sanskrit_shloka:
मय्यखण्डसुखाम्भोधौ बहुधा विश्ववीचयः ।
उत्पद्यन्ते विलीयन्ते मायामारुतविभ्रमात् ॥ ४९६ ॥
transliteration:
mayyakhaṇḍasukhāmbhodhau bahudhā viśvavīcayaḥ |
utpadyante vilīyante māyāmārutavibhramāt || 496 ||
translation: In me, the ocean of Infinite Bliss, the waves of the universe are created and destroyed by the playing of the wind of Māyā.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: In me, the ocean of Infinite Bliss, the waves of the universe are created and destroyed by the playing of the wind of Māyā.

sanskrit_shloka:
स्थुलादिभावा मयि कल्पिता भ्रमाद् आरोपितानुस्फुरणेन लोकैः ।
काले यथा कल्पकवत्सराय णर्त्वादयो निष्कलनिर्विकल्पे ॥ ४९७ ॥
transliteration:
sthulādibhāvā mayi kalpitā bhramād āropitānusphuraṇena lokaiḥ |
kāle yathā kalpakavatsarāya ṇartvādayo niṣkalanirvikalpe || 497 ||
translation: Such ideas as gross (or subtle) are erroneously imagined in me by people through the manifestation of things superimposed – just as in the indivisible and absolute time, cycles, years, half-years, seasons, etc., are imagined.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Such ideas as gross (or subtle) are erroneously imagined in me by people through the manifestation of things superimposed – just as in the indivisible and absolute time, cycles, years, half-years, seasons, etc., are imagined.

sanskrit_shloka:
आरोपितं नाश्रयदूषकं भवेत् कदापि मूढैरतिदोषदूषितैः ।
नार्द्रिकरोत्यूषरभूमिभागं मरीचिकावारि महाप्रवाहः ॥ ४९८ ॥
transliteration:
āropitaṃ nāśrayadūṣakaṃ bhavet kadāpi mūḍhairatidoṣadūṣitaiḥ |
nārdrikarotyūṣarabhūmibhāgaṃ marīcikāvāri mahāpravāhaḥ || 498 ||
translation: That which is superimposed by the grossly ignorant fools can never taint the substratum: The great rush of waters observed in a mirage never wets the desert tracts.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: That which is superimposed by the grossly ignorant fools can never taint the substratum: The great rush of waters observed in a mirage never wets the desert tracts.

sanskrit_shloka:
आकाशवल्लेपविदूरगोऽहं आदित्यवद्भास्यविलक्षणोऽहम् ।
अहार्यवन्नित्यविनिश्चलोऽहं अम्भोधिवत्पारविवर्जितोऽहम् ॥ ४९९ ॥
transliteration:
ākāśavallepavidūrago'haṃ ādityavadbhāsyavilakṣaṇo'ham |
ahāryavannityaviniścalo'haṃ ambhodhivatpāravivarjito'ham || 499 ||
translation: I am beyond contamination like the sky; I am distinct from things illumined, like the sun; I am always motionless like the mountain; I am limitless like the ocean.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: I am beyond contamination like the sky; I am distinct from things illumined, like the sun; I am always motionless like the mountain; I am limitless like the ocean.

sanskrit_shloka:
न मे देहेन संबन्धो मेघेनेव विहायसः ।
अतः कुतो मे तद्धर्मा जाक्रत्स्वप्नसुषुप्तयः ॥ ५00 ॥
transliteration:
na me dehena saṃbandho megheneva vihāyasaḥ |
ataḥ kuto me taddharmā jākratsvapnasuṣuptayaḥ || 500 ||
translation: I have no connection with the body, as the sky with clouds; so how can the states of wakefulness, dream and profound sleep, which are attributes of the body, affect me?
